transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t get this thought out of my head… that after all my years working as an electrician, I still couldn’t keep my own brother safe. And if that’s true, then maybe I’m a danger to anyone working with me, or even anyone living under my roof.
Do you feel like you have to do anything over and over to try and get rid of this thought about not being able to keep your brother safe?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I have some exact thing I do over and over to make it stop. The thought just comes back, and I get stuck with it.
Do you feel like you have to avoid certain things or situations because of this thought about not being able to keep your brother safe?

Yes. I avoid a lot now. I don’t go into my own garage unless I really have to. I stopped helping with the electrical work at church, which I used to do. And if people start talking about car projects or the fire, I cut it off pretty quick. I just can’t deal with it.
Do you feel like you're doing anything to prevent something bad from happening because of this thought about your brother?

I don’t know. I mean, I avoid things, like I said, but I don’t think I’m doing some specific thing to stop something bad from happening. It’s more like I just don’t trust myself around certain situations, so I stay away.
Do you ever feel like you have to think certain thoughts or say certain words to yourself to make the thought about not keeping your brother safe go away?

No, I don’t think so. I don’t have certain words or phrases I repeat to make it go away. It’s more like the thought hits me and I try to push it out or get away from whatever brought it up, but I’m not saying anything specific to myself.
Do you feel like you have to think or do something specific when the thought about not keeping your brother safe comes up, in order to feel better or less anxious?
Not really. I mean, I try to get away from it or distract myself, but I don’t have a specific thing I have to do or think to calm down. It’s more just… waiting for it to pass, I guess.
Do you feel like the thought about not keeping your brother safe comes into your mind against your will?

Yes. It comes in when I don’t want it to. I can be in the middle of wiring a panel, focused on the work, and all of a sudden I’m right back there—smelling smoke, seeing my brother. Or I’ll hear my nephew shut the garage door and it just hits me. It’s like everything around me drops out for a second.
Do you feel like you have to do something in response to the thought about not keeping your brother safe to try and make it less disturbing or to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think so. I don’t have some action I have to do to stop something bad from happening. When it comes up, I just get upset and try to get through it or shift my attention, but it’s not like a rule or ritual I have to follow.
Do you feel like you have to perform any specific actions when you have the thought about not keeping your brother safe?
No, I don’t think there’s any specific action I have to do. I might stop what I’m doing or try to distract myself, but it’s not like I have to do a certain thing every time.
Do you feel like there's something you must do when the thought about not keeping your brother safe comes up?
No… I don’t think there’s anything I must do. It’s more like I get hit with it and I try to steady myself, but I don’t have a specific thing I feel forced to do.
Do you feel upset or distressed when the thought about not keeping your brother safe comes into your mind?

Yeah. It hits me hard. I get this heavy guilt and anger in my chest, and it can sit there most of the day. It’s worse when I look at my nephew and think… he lost his dad, and now he’s stuck with me instead. That thought really messes me up.
Do you ever relive the moment of your brother's accident as if it's happening again?

Yeah. It can happen out of nowhere. I’ll be wiring a panel, or I’ll hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly it’s like I’m back there again—smelling smoke, seeing my brother. For a second it feels like the job site just drops out from under me.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the moment of your brother's accident as if it's happening again, like you're right back there?

Yeah… like I said, it does happen. I’ll be doing something normal, like wiring a panel, or I hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly I’m back there. I can smell the smoke, see my brother, and for a moment it’s like everything around me disappears.
Do you avoid talking about your brother or the accident with others?

Yeah. I don’t really talk about him or the accident if I can help it. If people start bringing up the fire, or even car projects, I shut it down pretty quick. I don’t go in my own garage unless I absolutely have to, and I stopped helping with the electrical stuff at church because it brings too much of it back.
Do you have nightmares about your brother's accident?

Yeah. Most nights I’m already lying there on edge, listening for sounds like crackling or a car door outside. And when I do sleep, I’ll have dreams about the garage… then I jolt awake soaked in sweat. After that I usually can’t get back to sleep before work.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and feelings about not keeping your brother safe?
About four months now. It started after the garage fire… and after my nephew came to live with us. Since then, those thoughts about not keeping my brother safe have just been there.
How long have you been avoiding things like going into your garage or talking about your brother and the accident?
It’s been about four months. Pretty much since the garage fire happened and my nephew came to live with us, I’ve been avoiding all of that.
How long have you been having nightmares about your brother's accident?
About four months. It started after the garage fire, around when my nephew came to live with us, and it’s been happening since then.
